newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS-Contract dispute to delay Malaysia Bakun dam.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Contract dispute to delay Malaysia Bakun dam.

text.p: A major dispute over construction contract terms is expected to delay Malaysia's $6.18 billion Bakun hydroelectric dam project, Acting Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said on Tuesday.

He said there were disagreements over "major terms" of the $5.5 billion engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contract between Ekran Bhd and one of the project's two main contractors, ABB Asea Brown Boveri.
"There has been conflict over the EPC agreement between Ekran and ABB and therefore, it would lead to some delay in the project," Anwar said. "The dispute is over major terms of the agreement.
He did not say how long the delay might be. The project is scheduled for completion by 2003.
"The estimates have been very, very conflicting ... of the total amount required. We plan to resolve this as soon as possible," Anwar said.
He added the hold-up in the project was also due to a delay in the diversion tunnel, being built to divert water away from the construction site.
Minister for Energy, Telecommunications and Posts Leo Moggie has been asked to intervene and resolve the issue, he said.
"Not only sub-contracting, I think the main agreement needs to be relooked at," Anwar said when asked if the dispute was over the awarding of sub-contracts.

ABB's portion of the work on Bakun includes supplying six 420 megawatt hydro-generators, a 500-kilovolt high voltage direct-current transmission system, installing a 650-km (400-mile) submarine cable to connect the dam to Peninsular Malaysia and civil works with joint contractor, Brazil's Companhia Brasileria Projectos e Obras (CBPO).
Ekran was the company to which the government awarded the contract. It has a 32 percent stake in Bakun Hydroelectric Corp Bhd (BHEC), the operating company of the project.

"There is (a) major review going on at the moment. Just now Ekran is in the process of having discussions with ABB. There are places (in the agreement) where it is not equitable," an official close to the project told Reuters.

He said the contract was negotiated when Ekran chairman Ting Pek Khiing was unwell in September last year. Many people involved in finalising the contract were not authorised to do so, which led to terms unfavourable to the Malaysian company.
"The terms that were not favourable are being reviewed," he said, but added that there was no fear of ABB pulling out of the contract.
Analysts were mixed in their response to the news.

"The impact (of a delay) on Ekran could be disastrous, as a lot of their earnings are due to come from the Bakun project," said Azman Mokhtar, associate research director at UBS Research in Kuala Lumpur.
But Linda Koh, research analyst at Phileo Allied Securities in in Kuala Lumpur said Ekran had already realised a lot of profits from the Bakun project.
Other analysts said the delay could also set back Bakun's listing plans, which could give underwriters more time to plan the placement in a bearish market.
Bakun is planning to issue 1.5 billion shares at two ringgit each.
At the lunch break on Tuesday, Ekran shares were down four cents at 4.8 ringgit on the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange. ($1 = 2.5 ringgit)
-- Kuala Lumpur newsroom (603-201 4813)
